update_log: Baseline initialization of high-frequency sports terminology frequently tested in competitive exams (SSC, Railways, State PSCs) for Sports Static GK.

cricket.meaning: A mode of dismissal where the ball strikes the batsman's leg before hitting the bat, and the umpire judges it would have hit the stumps.
An over consisting of six deliveries in which the batting team scores no runs.
A deceptive spinning delivery bowled by a leg-spin bowler that spins in the opposite direction (towards the right-handed batsman) to a normal leg-break.
A batsman being dismissed without scoring a single run. (A 'Golden Duck' is dismissal on the very first ball faced).
A fast delivery pitched right at the batsman's toes or the base of the stumps.
A fielding position placed extremely close to the batsman on the off-side.

football.meaning: A foul called when an attacking player is closer to the opponent's goal line than both the ball and the second-last defender when a pass is made to them.
When a single player scores three goals in a single match.
The skillful act of moving the ball past opponents with slight touches while retaining control.
A direct free kick taken from the penalty spot, awarded for a major foul committed inside the penalty area.

field_hockey.meaning: A method used to restart the game after a stoppage. Two opposing players face each other, tap their sticks on the ground and then against each other's stick.
A technique where the player lifts the ball off the ground by placing the head of the stick under it.
A set piece awarded to the attacking team for a defensive foul inside the penalty circle.
The synthetic artificial grass surface on which modern international hockey is played.

golf.meaning: Scoring one stroke under the par for a specific hole.
Scoring one stroke over the par for a specific hole.
A highly rare score of three strokes under par on a single hole.
The small wooden or plastic peg used to elevate the ball for the first shot of a hole. Also refers to the starting area.
The person who carries a golfer's clubs and provides assistance and advice during a match.

tennis_and_badminton.meaning: A tie score of 40-40 in a game, requiring a player to win two consecutive points to secure the game.
The point scored immediately after a deuce. If the player holding the advantage wins the next point, they win the game.
A call that requires the point to be replayed, typically when a serve hits the net cord but still lands in the correct service box.
A powerful, overhead shot hit steeply downward into the opponent's court.

chess.meaning: A position in which a player's king is under direct attack (in check) and there is no legal move to escape.
A situation where the player whose turn it is to move is not in check but has no legal moves. The game ends in a draw.
An opening move in which a player sacrifices a piece (usually a pawn) to secure an advantageous position.
A special defensive move involving the King and the Rook moving simultaneously.

boxing_and_wrestling.meaning: A winning condition where a fighter is knocked down and unable to rise before the referee counts to ten.
A boxer who leads with the right hand and right foot forward, typically a left-handed fighter.
A quick, straight punch thrown with the lead hand.
A wrestling term referring to lifting the opponent with effort.

billiards_and_snooker.meaning: The long, tapered wooden stick used to strike the ball.
Sinking an object ball into one of the pockets.
A foul committed when the cue ball accidentally falls into a pocket.
A shot in Billiards where the cue ball strikes both the other two balls on the table in a single shot.

other_prominent_terms.meaning: A highly strenuous swimming technique where both arms move symmetrically over the water while the legs perform a dolphin kick.
An offensive play where one player throws the ball near the basket and a teammate jumps, catches it in mid-air, and scores.
The shape of the baseball field marked by the four bases.
